question.worked_solution:
The multiplicative property of modular congruences states that if

$$
a≡b\,\text{and}\,c≡d\,(\text{mod}\,n),
$$

then, we have 

$$
ac≡bd\,(\text{mod}\,n).
$$

First, we note the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}124 & ≡24\cdot 5+4\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡24\cdot 0+4\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡4\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\ 99 & ≡19\cdot 5+4\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡19\cdot 0+4\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡4\, & (\text{mod}\,5)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by the multiplicative property of congruences, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}124\cdot 99 & ≡4\cdot 4\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡16\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡3\cdot 5+1\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡3\cdot 0+1\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡0+1\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡1\, & (\text{mod}\,5)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
124\cdot 99\text{ mod }5=1.
$$
